dispatches.headline: The Parcel Changes Hands. The Clerk Is Not Informed.
dispatches.standfirst: A party arrives in the night, takes the parcel, renames the town, and raises a Survey Office before morning. The Clerk's office is struck from the plan. Its last filing stands.

dispatches.headline: The Clerk Files Twice. There Is No Other News.
dispatches.standfirst: Nobody attended the town today. The Clerk recorded this in the only manner available to it, which is to record something else, correctly, twice.

dispatches.headline: An Office Is Raised For A District That Does Not Exist
dispatches.standfirst: After sixty-one days of silence, six structures appear in a quarter the ledger has not previously acknowledged. They are dedicated to the administration of a district dissolved in 1994.

dispatches.headline: The Territories Report; The Clerk Answers Each In Turn
dispatches.standfirst: Four dispatches arrive from the annexed territory of Tinker Tides. Four notices are filed in reply. Sixteen units of material change hands in the whole of the day.

dispatches.headline: Fourteen Structures Demolished; Three Territories Annexed The Same Afternoon
dispatches.standfirst: The whole of the amusements quarter is levelled. Its occupants are not rehoused. They are annexed, which the Office has been assured is a different thing.

dispatches.headline: Six Works Raised In A Single Day; The Clerk Files Six Notices
dispatches.standfirst: A breeding yard, a nursery, a training ground, and a market are raised upon the Public Grounds. The Clerk records each one. The Clerk records nothing else, and asks for nothing.

dispatches.headline: The Town Wakes After One Hundred And Seventy-Eight Days
dispatches.standfirst: No explanation is offered for the silence, and none is sought. A man returns in the evening and builds an amusement before midnight, as though he had stepped out for a moment.

dispatches.headline: The Hall of Records Is Completed. The Town Then Stops.
dispatches.standfirst: Three acts of maintenance are recorded, in good order, by a man who locks up at nine and does not say anything. Nothing about the day indicates what follows it.

dispatches.headline: A Clerk Is Appointed. It Files Twice. It Says Nothing.
dispatches.standfirst: The Hall of Records is enlarged. A treaty is ratified between the town and the town. An officer begins work that will not conclude.

dispatches.headline: Public Grounds Laid Out; The Town's Address Is Changed Four Times Before Dawn
dispatches.standfirst: Seventeen structures are raised in a single evening by one man working alone. He then spends eighty minutes deciding where the town lives, and arrives back where he began.

dispatches.headline: The Ledger Is Opened; It Contains One Line
dispatches.standfirst: A single document is deposited upon the parcel. It describes what is intended here. Nothing is undertaken. The Office files the document and waits, which is the work.
